Starting point
AI system and date: ChatGPT November 3rd, 2026.
Before using AI for the required extension, briefly state your question, course-based core model, baseline result, and the specific limitation or opportunity you wanted to address.
This statistical analysis of social anxiety data, seeks to answer the research question: How is a person’s lifestyle behaviors related to the intensity of their social anxiety level? To answer this questions we ran a multiple regression analysis with social anxiety levels as the response variable representing social anxiety level and sleep hours, physical activity, caffeine intake, alcohol consumption, and diet quality as the predictor variables representing lifestyle behaviors. Based on our preliminary results, holding all other predictors constant, sleep hours, physical activity, and diet quality were negatively associated, while caffeine intake and alcohol consumption were positively associated with social anxiety levels. One potential limitation is multicollinearity between predictor variables alcohol consumption and diet quality, as well as between caffeine intake and sleep hours.

My decisions

Accepted: What useful advice did you use?

The preferred extension is a sensitivity analysis that runs an ordinal logistic regression to determine whether treating our response variable as ordered categorical data would change our conclusions about the association between lifestyle behaviors and social anxiety levels.

Changed: What did you adapt to fit your data or goals?

We requested an updated suggestion list based on topics learned in class, so that we could choose from a list of extensions that could stretched us beyond class content.

Rejected or corrected: What advice was unsuitable, unnecessary, or wrong?

Multicollinearity diagnostics and sensitivity analysis, (redundant with Selection and Shrinkage)
Investigate nonlinear relationships using polynomial regression, (learned in class)
Interactive application, (this extension does not strengthen the model)
Random forest and interpretation


Connection to the final case study: This sensitivity analysis would be placed right after finishing our cross-validation and we have fitted our final model. Our multiple linear regression would be strengthen by this extension because it addresses the likely case that out response variable of social anxiety level is not a discrete variable but an ordinal variable where intervals between 1 to 2 do not mean the same as the interval 9 to 10 for example. Throught this sensitivity analysis we could have a interpretation of our data considering this variable type and see if the conclusions would be similar or different from our multiple linear regression.

title: Factors Associated with Anxiety Levels
text:
The question
In one or two short paragraphs, introduce the setting, audience, focused research question, data source, observational unit, response, important predictors, and one important data limitation. Lead with what makes the question worth answering.

Our research question is: How are a person’s lifestyle behaviors related to the intensity of their social anxiety? Our intended audience includes clinicians, researchers interested in social anxiety, and individuals experiencing social anxiety. Finding and understanding the association between daily lifestyle behaviors and social anxiety levels can be helpful for understanding how these factors are related. Our findings could also support current and future experimental studies that seek to investigate causal relationships.


We are using the Social Anxiety Dataset by Zhang (2024), which contains 11,000 observations, with each observation representing a recorded individual. Our response variable is social anxiety level, measured on a scale from 1 to 10. From an initial pool of 11 candidate predictors, we selected five lifestyle behaviors related to personal decisions: sleep hours, physical activity, caffeine intake, alcohol consumption, and diet quality. One important limitation is that the dataset is described as being based on real-world surveys and observational studies, but having gone through preprocessing and cleaning for analytical use. Because of this, the relationships between lifestyle habits and social anxiety may not accurately reflect the relationships we would observe in real life. The creator of the data set strongly recommends using the data for research and educational purposes only, not to diagnose or assign treatment to patients. Nevertheless, with the data available we aim to find the association of our selected lifestyle habits and its associated social stress intensity level. Additionally, the data was collected through self-reported surveys and observational studies, which may result in possible non-response sampling bias if those who chose not to participate in the surveys or observations are significantly different than the sampled population.

Holding physical activity, caffeine intake, alcohol consumption, and dietary quality constant, an increase in one hour of sleep is associated with a predicted decrease of about 0.6875 points in social anxiety level, on average.


We are 95% confident that, holding the other predictors constant, each additional hour of sleep is associated with a decrease of between 0.660 and 0.715 points in the mean social anxiety level.


One possible limitation is multicollinearity, because some lifestyle predictors might be related. For example, caffeine intake could be related to the number of hours slept, and alcohol consumption could also be related to dietary quality. This might make our standard errors bigger and make it harder to interpret each predictor’s individual relationship with anxiety levels.



Show code
avPlots(anxiety_fit)










The added-variable plots show each predictor’s relationship with social anxiety levels after accounting for the other predictors in our regression model. Sleep hours appear to have the strongest negative relationship with social anxiety, while caffeine intake shows a positive relationship. Physical activity, alcohol consumption, and diet quality show weaker relationships.

title: Factors Associated with Anxiety Levels
text:
A new direction with AI

The original need was to address a potential multicollinearity, however the AI support helped identified a potential reinterpretation of our response variable. Since the measurement of social anxiety level is not described, the response variable might represent an ordinal variable instead of a continuous variable. For example, an intervals between 1 to 2 and 9 to 10 could differ substantially. This made us question whether treating social anxiety levels as continuous in our original multiple linear regression model was the most appropriate approach. Therefore for the extension we will run an ordinal logistic regression to determine if that would change our conclusions about the association between lifestyle behaviors and social anxiety levels.


After fitting the ordinal logistic regression model, we will compare its findings with our original model to see whether the relationships we observed remain similar. To verify our extension, we plan to check the proportional-odds assumption using ordinal::nominal_test() and validate the predicted probabilities using predict() to make sure they are between 0 and 1 and sum to 1.
